display.title: Episode 37: Three Lost on an Island, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: The doctor, the scientist and the engineer save a sick queen, and the king must decide who earns the greatest reward: a parable about the body and the neshama.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by thanking the many families who listen and explaining that Hashem's blessing comes through simcha, followed by a lively march. Story time recaps the three survivors on the island and their discoveries, and a young guest in Studio 604 leads the Shema. Through the telescope the scientist sees a castle with a sign: the queen is very sick, and whoever cures her will be richly rewarded. The three fly there, and the doctor's apple cures the queen, but each claims the whole reward, including the hand of the king's daughter. The king gives each a fortune and his daughter to the doctor, because the airplane and telescope are no longer needed while the apple must be kept. Uncle Yossi explains the parable: our needs, our body and our neshama all matter, but the great reward goes to the neshama, since only Torah and good deeds accompany a person to the next world (Pirkei Avos), and Hashem, Torah and Yisroel are one (Zohar). The mailbox answers a girl who just turned twelve: she can stay in Tzivos Hashem. The show ends with the children's Sefer Torah campaign.
display.lesson: Body and possessions serve the neshama; only Torah and mitzvos go with us forever, so put your main effort there.
